ops.title: SocketBoundedChannelTests.expectCanceledFullSendSettles can silently stop testing its subject
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 during the Swift flake work; both the implementer and its refuter confirmed it and
both declined to fix it unilaterally. Recorded rather than fixed, per the refuter's recommendation.

`SocketBoundedChannelTests.swift:48` uses `await Task.yield()` as a synchronisation primitive: it
assumes one yield parks the producer inside `send`. If the producer has not parked yet,
`producer.cancel()` takes the early-cancel path instead of the stranded-when-full path. Both return
`false`, so the assertion passes either way and the test goes green while covering neither the case
it names nor the case it intended.

This is a **silent coverage loss, not a flake** — it never turns CI red, which is why it can rot
indefinitely. It is the same family as the nine `/bin/true` assertions and the `exec sleep 600` that
hid a forked-descendant defect: a test that passes for a reason other than the one it claims.

Why it was not fixed in that pass: closing it properly wants a `senderCount` or a parked-sender hook
on the production type, and that pass had just deleted two dead test seams (`openCommitHook`,
`requestWriteStartHook`) for having zero callers. Adding a new production seam for a test in the same
change would be the exact irony that justified deleting them.

Options for whoever takes it: expose a parked-sender observation on the channel and wait on it; or
rename the test to what it actually covers and write a separate one for the stranded path.

ops.text: The test either observes the producer parked in send, or is renamed to what it actually covers
